claims.claim: Top-line readiness parity can hide controller dependence in local MLX Gemma tool-use runs.
claims.primary_metric: H1h/H1i no-directive readiness parity with high repair/fallback burden and low raw-clean rate.
claims.limitation: Current support is internal to Moonie's knowledge-work harness and local MLX runtime.
claims.next_test: Run the same helper-ablation structure on a harder H1 slice selected from raw replay failures.

claims.claim: The final tool-turn directive is causal for exact raw tool protocol behavior on the focused replay suite.
claims.primary_metric: Contracted exact replay is 7/8 while no-directive exact replay is 0/8 on the same cases.
claims.limitation: The replay suite is intentionally focused on eight observed no-directive failures, not a population estimate.
claims.next_test: Expand the replay suite with independently authored hard cases and repeated seeds.

claims.claim: Packaged workflow completion can wash out raw one-turn tool-protocol failures.
claims.primary_metric: H1j/H1k packaged packets saturated while exact replay still showed no-directive failures.
claims.limitation: The packaged workflow scaffolds may make the task easier than the one-turn replay contract.
claims.next_test: Build a harder packaged workflow slice that preserves one-turn parallel and visual follow-on pressure.

claims.claim: Tool-catalog role presentation changes visual routing behavior even without the exact tool-turn directive.
claims.primary_metric: visual_role_catalog_v1 moves latest-filter from wrong/no-call behavior to refine_selection argument mismatch.
claims.limitation: The intervention improves routing more than exact literal fidelity.
claims.next_test: Test catalog-role profiles across a larger visual follow-on set with fresh UI states.

claims.claim: Schema-local visual argument hints improve exact selector fidelity but can hurt executable visual-form recovery.
claims.primary_metric: v2 reaches 2/3 focused visual live exactness but loses executable form-target recovery.
claims.limitation: The improvement is focused on three visual replay cases and has a known form-target regression.
claims.next_test: Search for a split selector intervention that preserves v2 filter exactness and v1 form-target executability.

claims.claim: Adding broader split-selector wording did not recover the missing visual-form behavior and introduced a protocol-shape regression.
claims.primary_metric: v3 raw exact falls to 1/8 versus v2 at 2/8 and readback regresses through tool_name/name mismatch.
claims.limitation: This is one candidate profile; it does not rule out all field-specific selector interventions.
claims.next_test: Try an executor-grounded schema annotation or few-shot-free field contract that does not add broad behavioral prose.

claims.claim: Schema-local visual field hints are cleaner than broad selector prose but still do not recover executable form targeting.
claims.primary_metric: v4 ties v2 at 2/8 raw exact and preserves readback, but stays 0/1 executable and over-prefers refine_selection on form-target.
claims.limitation: This tests one schema-field annotation profile on the focused eight-case replay-derived probe.
claims.next_test: Create a fresh visual hard slice or constrain refine_selection preference only when a real selection_id is present.

claims.claim: The next visual hard slice should separate visible-region targeting, valid selection carryover, compact filter copying, and protocol-shape readback.
claims.primary_metric: Eight fresh planned cases across visual argument copying, routing, referent carryover, and region readback.
claims.limitation: This packet is an eval design artifact; it is not model-performance evidence until run against candidate rows.
claims.next_test: Implement the designed cases as a replayable visual hard-slice packet, then compare contracted, no-directive, v1, v2, and any refine-selection-gated candidate.
